mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals stronger household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not statistically higher than baseline during periods of GDPC1 growth > 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 6% signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressure and boosts corporate margins, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically higher than baseline during UNRATE < 6% episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 1% signals stronger manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically higher than baseline during INDPRO growth > 1% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a successful disinflationary tightening, which reduces long-term interest rates and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not statistically higher than baseline during FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below -1% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically lower than baseline during RSAFS < -1% months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) below 50,000 signals weak labor market momentum, which reduces earnings growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically lower than baseline during PAYEMS < 50,000 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) and decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals a shift from construction to manufacturing, which boosts earnings expectations in cyclical sectors and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not statistically higher than baseline during INDPRO rises and HOUST falls (t-test p > 0.05).
